content.title: ‘Paradise’ season 2 finale explained: Did [spoiler] die?
content.text: Season 2 of Hulu’s “Paradise” has come to an end, answering some of viewers’ burning questions and setting up new ones for season 3. Warning: Spoilers ahead for season 2 of “Paradise.”Thus far on “Paradise,” most of the action has taken place within a city-sized underground bunker built to withstand an extinction-level event. That’s about to change, because the bunker was destroyed during the season 2 finale, which premiered on Monday, March 30.All the inhabitants managed to escape before the bunker’s nuclear reactors exploded, except for one person: Samantha “Sinatra” Redmond (Julianne Nicholson), the billionaire who spearheaded its construction.Here’s everything you need to know about the “Paradise” season 2 finale:Did Sinatra die in ‘Paradise’?Sinatra knew that someone had to stay inside the doomed bunker to close the doors, protecting everyone outside from the explosion. She chose to sacrifice herself.“Paradise” executive producer John Hoberg, who co-wrote the season 2 finale, confirmed to The Hollywood Reporter that Sinatra is dead.Julianne Nicholson as Samantha "Sinatra" Redmond.Disney“What we wanted to do was redeem her to some degree. Whether or not you fully feel she’s redeemed or not, we wanted to get her to the point where you’re like, ‘I understand. She did some terrible things, but she thinks it’s all in the service of saving the world. Some of these small choices that are atrocious were for the larger good,’” Hoberg said.The writer also said fans shouldn’t rule out the possibility of Nicholson reprising her role in season 3 of “Paradise.” ​​”It’s a [Dan] Fogelman show, so you never know. You might see somebody from the past,” Hoberg teased.What’s going on with time travel in ‘Paradise’?One of the central mysteries of season 2 was the identity of Alex. It turns out Alex was not a human, but an A.I.-controlled quantum computer. Link (Thomas Doherty), who leads a group of survivors outside the bunker, actually invented Alex back when he was auditing courses at Caltech.READ MORE: Is ‘Paradise’ ending after season 3?Link teamed up with one of his professors, quantum scientist Henry Miller (Patrick Fischler), to further develop the technology. Sinatra eventually hired Henry, seeking to use Alex’s extraordinary predictive qualities to help save the world.During the season 2 finale, Miller told Sinatra that they needed to shut down Alex because it was “trying to manipulate time.” He informed her that Alex had provided a solution in 10 seconds that would have taken a “supercomputer longer than the age of the universe to solve.” The most chilling part? Miller hadn’t even asked the question yet.Thomas Doherty as Link in "Paradise."DisneyBy the end of season 2, Sinatra was convinced that time manipulation had already taken place. She believed that Link, whose real name is Dylan, was actually her son who died as a child. She also hinted that Secret Service agent Xavier Collins (Sterling K. Brown) had already saved the bunker’s inhabitants in a separate timeline.Before sacrificing herself, Sinatra told Xavier that he had to travel to a second bunker 100 miles away.“It houses a quantum computer that can stop all of this. In fact, it already has stopped all of this. You just need to get there,” Sinatra said. When Xavier asked why he should carry out the enormous task, Sinatra replied, “I believe you already have.” As for whether Sinatra’s time travel theory is real, Hoberg says viewers will have to wait and see.READ MORE: Here’s every show that’s been canceled and renewed in 2026 so far“Maybe Sinatra is crazy, and Alex isn’t really doing this, but she sure feels like Dylan could be proof that this is actually working,” he said. “Sinatra was certain enough that she was at peace when she was walking through her crumbling bunker city. There’s just a lot more to unpack about whether that’s the reality of all of that.”Is Link really Sinatra’s son Dylan?Hoberg said it’s supposed to be ambiguous whether Link is actually Sinatra’s son. “You should be able to decide for yourself whether you think Sinatra’s gone a little crazy. Is this her son or is it not? One thing that’s very important to us is that the show is trying to stay slightly agnostic about it, while also leading [you in] a direction,” he said. Seasons 1 and 2 of “Paradise” are available to stream on Hulu.
